Article Title: EPFO approves SWP for retirees to withdraw PF savings in regular instalments; relaxes minimum balance to 10%
Article Text:
According to the EPFO, the initiative will strengthen financial security after retirement.

What is EPFO’s SWP for your PF account?

Minimum balance requirements and more

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

In a big move that will benefit lakhs of provident fund subscribers, the Central Board of Trustees (CBT) has approved a proposal to introduce a Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) for retiring members of the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation ( EPFO ). The Times of India had first reported about the proposal being under consideration today. Under the proposed facility, members will be able to receive their accumulated provident fund savings in instalments over a period of time instead of taking out the entire amount at once.Under the proposed facility, retirees will be able to choose the frequency of their withdrawals, with options including monthly, quarterly and half-yearly payments.This will give members a structured source of regular income while allowing the balance of their provident fund corpus to remain invested and continue generating returns, the government release said.Participation in the scheme will be entirely voluntary, and members will not be required to opt for periodic withdrawals.The facility may also be extended to eligible family members and beneficiaries, offering households greater flexibility and financial protection.The objectives include ensuring a steady income after retirement, lowering reinvestment risks, supporting the sustainability of the fund and widening social security coverage to gig and platform workers.The SWP will allow retirees to receive predictable payments from their accumulated savings without giving up ownership of the remaining corpus.In the initial phase, around 6.32 lakh EPF members aged above 55 years, each with provident fund savings of over Rs 5 lakh, are expected to be the main beneficiaries of the proposed arrangement.If a member dies while receiving SWP payments, the nominee or dependent will be able to either withdraw the outstanding balance or continue receiving instalments.To offer greater flexibility and advance the objective of universal social security, the proposal also envisages UAN-linked facilities for direct voluntary deposits and small contributions from third parties, including customer tips.These payments will be possible independently of conventional employer payroll systems.The required amendments to the EPF Scheme will be notified after approval from the Ministry. A corresponding amendment to the Income Tax Act is being taken up with the Ministry of Finance.The board approved revisions to the minimum balance and waiting period provisions governing withdrawals.Under the earlier arrangement, members were required to retain 25% of their contributions in their accounts as a minimum balance at all times.The prescribed minimum has now been lowered from 25% to 10%.The waiting period for withdrawal has also been cut from 12 months to two months.These changes are intended to give EPF members greater access to their money while continuing to protect their long-term social security interests.The board also cleared amendments to the EDLI Scheme, 2026, to help resolve pending legacy exemption cases and give eligible establishments six months to renew exemptions that have expired.
Article Summary: The Central Board of Trustees (CBT) has approved a proposal to introduce a Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) for retiring members of the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation ( EPFO ). The Times of India had first reported about the proposal being under consideration today.

Article Title: Hallmarked gold faces a purity test as India Bullion and Jewellers Association has flagged alleged adulteration using rhenium powder, fabricated gold purity reports through jeweller-hallmarking centre
Article Text:
Following the industry body’s representation, the BIS has convened a meeting on November 23 to discuss the concerns in detail. (Image for representative purpose only)

Gold hallmarking concerns

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Gold prices are crashing and if you think this is a good time to buy jewellery, be alert about hallmarking in gold. Concerns have emerged over the credibility of India’s BIS certification system following allegations of widespread irregularities in gold hallmarking and refining.The India Bullion and Jewellers Association (IBJA) has raised suspicions of collusion between jewellers and hallmarking centres, fabricated purity reports, kickbacks linked to fees and sophisticated methods of adulterating gold using rhenium powder, according to an ET report.In a representation submitted to the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), the association highlighted discrepancies in Hallmark Unique Identification (HUID) data displayed on the BIS Care app, along with the operations of unregistered refiners.It warned that shortcomings in regulatory monitoring could leave consumers vulnerable to financial losses and weaken confidence in hallmarked gold. The IBJA has called for surprise inspections, stricter testing procedures and stringent action against hallmarking centres and refiners found violating the rules.Following the industry body’s representation, the BIS has convened a meeting on November 23 to discuss the concerns in detail.India consumes around 800-850 tonnes of gold annually.The IBJA has also called on the BIS to bring nearly 4,000 unregistered gold refiners operating in India under its regulatory oversight. It alleged that the lack of supervision over these entities is enabling impure gold to enter the jewellery supply chain, creating the possibility of such gold reaching consumers.Surendra Mehta, national secretary of the India Bullion and Jewellers Association (IBJA), told ET that numerous businesses operating as gold refiners were neither registered with the BIS nor answerable to any regulatory body.He alleged that many of these operators were merely melting gold rather than refining it, resulting in impure metal entering the market through jewellers as gold bars, coins and jewellery.“These unregistered refiners make impure gold and operate in the same way fake currency notes are made and circulated,” Mehta said, stressing the need for stricter oversight of the gold refining industry.The IBJA has urged the BIS to bring every unregistered refiner under its supervision. It has also called for jewellers to be allowed to source gold bars and coins only from refiners accredited by the BIS and the National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories. The association has advised consumers and investors to buy gold bars and coins from accredited refiners to reduce the chances of purchasing adulterated gold.The representation comes against the backdrop of increasing industry concern over allegations that rhenium powder, reportedly sourced from China, is being mixed with gold to add weight to jewellery. There are concerns that this form of adulteration could go undetected during standard hallmarking checks, prompting questions about whether current testing procedures are adequate.The Gem & Jewellery Export Promotion Council (GJEPC) has also looked into the technical aspects of the alleged adulteration. It has written to the BIS seeking an official clarification on whether rhenium can be used to adulterate gold and whether hallmarking centres need to strengthen their testing methods.Rhenium is a refractory metal with a melting point of more than 3,100 degrees Celsius. At the temperatures typically used in jewellery manufacturing, around 1,050-1,100 degrees Celsius, it cannot melt or dissolve in gold.
Article Summary: Concerns have emerged over the credibility of India’s BIS certification system. India Bullion and Jewellers Association (IBJA) has raised suspicions of collusion between jewellers and hallmarking centres. The BIS has convened a meeting on November 23 to discuss the concerns in detail.

Article Title: What's next for Anthropic shares - will it boom or pop?
Article Text:
Anthropic's record-breaking IPO raises questions over the sustainability of the AI boom as costs, regulation and safety concerns loom

Revenue is soaring, but so are costs

Data centres and regulation could weigh on shares

Anthropic's safety pledge faces scrutiny

What's next for Anthropic?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Anthropic's record-breaking stock market debut has put the artificial intelligence company at the centre of a new debate over whether the AI boom can sustain its momentum. The maker of Claude chatbot ended its first day of trading on Thursday with a market valuation of around $1.75 trillion, after raising $81 billion in what was reported as the largest initial public offering ( IPO ) in history. But concerns over the industry's high spending, mounting risks and market volatility have raised questions about what lies ahead for its shares.The stock surged as much as 34% after trading began before closing about 17% above its IPO price at just over $97. The debut has made Anthropic one of the world's most valuable companies, but investors will now be watching whether the rally holds and how the company manages its growing costs, infrastructure investments and safety commitments.Why the AI market remains under pressureAnthropic's debut comes at a time when investor confidence in the broader AI industry remains unsettled. Major US stock indexes fell to seven-month lows on Thursday, while Asian markets also saw sharp declines in early trading on Friday.Despite the strong demand for Anthropic shares, analysts say its debut alone may not be enough to reassure investors about the long-term outlook for AI companies.Anthropic's rapid growth has been reflected in its revenue. According to its investor prospectus, the company generated $16.2 billion in revenue in the first six months of 2026, compared with $4.6 billion for the whole of 2025.However, the company has also reported substantial losses, including a reported $80 billion loss in the first half of 2026, largely attributed to a one-off charge. Its losses reportedly reached $104 billion in the first nine months of 2026.Anthropic is expected to spend heavily on infrastructure as it expands its AI operations. The company has plans to spend around $900 billion on data centre infrastructure over the next two decades, raising concerns about the scale of capital it may need to sustain its growth.The IPO provides the company with fresh capital for these investments, but analysts expect spending requirements and financing needs to remain a key concern for investors.Anthropic's expansion also comes amid growing opposition to AI infrastructure, particularly data centres, in the US. Protests against proposed data centre projects have gained momentum, with some municipalities and states voting for restrictions or bans.The company's growth is closely tied to investments in the infrastructure that powers AI tools such as Claude. A slowdown in data centre spending could have implications not just for Anthropic but also for the wider US economy.Regulatory scrutiny is another factor investors will be watching. Senior Democrats have signalled the possibility of tighter oversight of AI companies, citing concerns over the risks posed by advanced AI systems and the volatility that large AI IPOs could introduce into financial markets.Last month, Senator Elizabeth Warren wrote to Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, warning that the company's IPO “could inject extreme volatility and risk into the financial system, which threatens to undermine Americans' economic security.”Anthropic was founded in 2021 by seven former OpenAI employees, including CEO Dario Amodei and his sister Daniela Amodei, who is the company's president. The founders left OpenAI with a focus on prioritising safety in AI development.The company has repeatedly warned about the potential risks of advanced AI, even as it continues to develop increasingly powerful models. In a recent filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Anthropic devoted 93 pages to risk factors, including the possibility that advanced AI systems could pose “catastrophic or existential risks to humanity.”However, the company's safety commitments have also come under scrutiny. Researcher Jacob Coxon resigned in September, criticising the safety practices of both Anthropic and OpenAI and arguing that the industry was moving too quickly.Amodei has called for a slowdown in AI development and advocated greater coordination between companies and countries, along with independent evaluations of AI systems.Speaking at the Nasdaq opening bell on Thursday, Amodei said the company's “most difficult safety work lies ahead of us”.“And to state it unequivocally, we will pace the training and deployment of AI systems, taking as long as is necessary to have confidence that they are safe and will remain under human control,” he said.The tension between Anthropic's safety commitments and its commercial ambitions is likely to remain a key issue as the company enters public markets.Anthropic's performance in the coming months will depend on whether it can sustain its growth while managing rising infrastructure costs, regulatory scrutiny and concerns over the risks of advanced AI. The company's expansion is also tied to data centre investments, which have faced growing opposition in the US, with some municipalities and states voting for restrictions or bans.Regulatory oversight could add another layer of uncertainty. Senior Democrats have signalled the possibility of tighter scrutiny of AI companies over the risks posed by advanced AI systems and the volatility large IPOs could introduce into financial markets.Anthropic's safety commitments are also likely to remain under scrutiny. The company has repeatedly warned about the risks of advanced AI even as it continues to develop increasingly powerful models. CEO Dario Amodei said at the Nasdaq opening bell on Thursday that the company's “most difficult safety work lies ahead of us”.The debut could also offer a signal for other AI firms planning to enter public markets. OpenAI, Anthropic's major rival, is expected to pursue an IPO in 2027. CEO Sam Altman said earlier this week that the company would go ahead with its IPO next year despite market volatility, adding, “There's been way too much investor demand and not enough supply.”
Article Summary: Anthropic's record-breaking IPO raises questions over the sustainability of the AI boom as costs, regulation and safety concerns loom. The maker of Claude chatbot ended its first day of trading on Thursday with a market valuation of around $1.75 trillion. The stock surged as much as 34% after trading began before closing about 17% above its IPO price at just over $97.

Anthropic briefly reached a valuation of around $2 trillion during its Nasdaq debut on Thursday, placing the five-year-old artificial intelligence company among the world's most valuable listed businesses. Its shares later pared their gains, leaving it with a closing fully diluted valuation of about $1.8 trillion, according to Bloomberg.The company’s shares opened at $111.50, around 34% above the initial public offering ( IPO ) price of $83. They closed at $97.17, up 17% from the offer price, Reuters reported. At the opening price, Anthropic’s fully diluted valuation — calculated using approximately 18 billion shares, including employee stock options and restricted stock units — touched about $2 trillion.Based on its closing price, Bloomberg ranked Anthropic as the world’s seventh most valuable publicly traded company. Six companies were valued higher: Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia, Alphabet, Amazon and SpaceX.Here's the list of top 10 most valuable publicly traded companies. Figures represent fully diluted market valuations.The listing marks a sharp rise from Anthropic’s valuation of $183 billion around 14 months ago.The company had initially sought a valuation of slightly more than $1 trillion when it began its IPO roadshow earlier in November, according to Reuters.The stock’s early surge was followed by profit-taking, as investors weighed the company’s prospects against concerns over high AI valuations, infrastructure spending and the sector’s long-term profitability."The blockbuster Anthropic launch is a critical step in reassuring the market about the potential for AI, but it's really just the beginning," Bob O'Donnell, chief analyst at TECHnalysis Research, told Reuters."We still need to see what happens with OpenAI, how the Nvidia situation evolves, how the political climate for data centers shapes up, and what the historical performance for Anthropic proves to be before we'll get any real sense of stability," he added.Led by chief executive Dario Amodei, a former OpenAI employee, Anthropic has positioned itself around AI safety while seeking to build a profitable business despite substantial computing costs. Reuters reported that its revenue rose 47% in the third quarter from the previous quarter, while its net loss narrowed. The company also has nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with partners, including Amazon and Google.Speaking to CNBC on Thursday, Amodei said, "At some point in the future we're hoping to be investment grade, and debt is an instrument that we have available to us, and we'd like to use at some point in the future."Anthropic’s performance as a public company will now be watched closely as investors assess its ability to convert rapid revenue growth into sustainable profits and manage its significant computing commitments.
Article Summary: Anthropic briefly reached a valuation of around $2 trillion during its Nasdaq debut on Thursday. The company’s shares opened at $111.50, around 34% above the initial public offering ( IPO ) price of $83.50. They closed at $97.17, up 17% from the offer price, Reuters reported.

Article Title: Anthropic CFO Krishna Rao joins billionaire club as shareholding tops $1 bn
Article Text:
Krishna Rao, chief financial officer of Anthropic PBC, right, during the Anthropic PBC initial public offering (IPO) at the Nasdaq MarketSite in New York, US, on Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026. Anthropic PBC awarded $550 million to the Wall Street banks working on its blockbuster IPO - more than they made on SpaceX, the previous title holder for the biggest debut ever. Photographer: Michael Nagle/Bloomberg

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Bengaluru: Krishna Rao, Indian-origin chief financial officer of Anthropic, has joined the billionaire club, with his shareholding in the artificial intelligence company valued at about $1.06 billion at a listing share price of $111.50.Rao holds about 9.5 million shares in Anthropic, according to the company’s updated IPO prospectus filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission. He is not among the shareholders selling shares in the IPO, and his holding will remain unchanged after the offering.A Yale and Harvard alumnus, Rao joined Anthropic as CFO in April 2024. Under the company’s 2021 Stock Plan, he was granted options to buy 14 million shares of Class A common stock at an exercise price of $1.30 per share. The options expire on May 30, 2034.As of December last year, he held 5.7 million exercisable options and another 8.16 million unexercisable options. During 2025, he exercised options covering 76,980 shares, realising $385,285.Rao received a salary of $706,250 in 2025, along with $14,000 in other compensation, taking his total compensation to $720,250. He did not receive any stock or option awards during the year, according to the company’s executive compensation disclosure.Before joining Anthropic, Rao was CFO of Fanatics Commerce, an online sports merchandise and retail platform, from May 2023 to April 2024. He previously served as CFO of healthcare technology company Cedar from July 2021 to May 2023.Between October 2015 and July 2021, he held several roles at Airbnb, including global head of corporate and business development and director of financial planning and analysis. Before that, he was a principal in the private equity group at Blackstone from September 2011 to September 2015. He began his career as a strategy consultant at Bain, where he worked from September 2005 to July 2008.

He is not among the shareholders selling shares in the IPO, and his holding will remain unchanged after the offering. Anthropic PBC awarded $550 million to the Wall Street banks working on its blockbuster IPO - more than they made on SpaceX.

Article Title: DGCA issues show-cause notice to SpiceJet over flight cancellations, operational lapses
Article Text:
Delhi airport flags possible flight disruptions over SpiceJet's ‘operational challenges’

Violations of international flight norms, route guidelines

SpiceJet's market share falls, shares decline

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Delhi airport warns passengers of flight disruptions

NEW DELHI: The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has issued a show-cause notice to crisis-hit SpiceJet seeking an explanation for rising flight cancellations, operational disruptions and alleged regulatory violations, news agency PTI reported citing sources.In the notice dated November 17, the aviation regulator flagged the airline's deteriorating operational performance, declining on-time performance (OTP), increasing flight delays and cancellations, and failure to adhere to its approved flight schedule.The DGCA also raised concerns over passenger inconvenience caused by disruptions and delays, as well as inadequate passenger facilitation measures. SpiceJet has been directed to respond within seven days of the notice.The regulator said a majority of SpiceJet's aircraft remain grounded and that the airline has failed to submit a credible plan for their return to service."... the majority of the aircraft fleet of SpiceJet is grounded and the airline has failed to submit a credible plan for return to service of the grounded aircraft," the DGCA said.The notice also flagged uncertainty over the renewal of mandatory insurance coverage and concerns raised by overseas aviation authorities over operational disruptions allegedly linked to delayed payments to service providers.The regulator further sought an explanation for SpiceJet's failure to pay a penalty imposed earlier, despite repeated reminders.The DGCA said SpiceJet had failed to meet eligibility requirements for scheduled international operations and had repeatedly violated Route Dispersal Guidelines (RDG), despite previous enforcement action.The regulator had imposed a penalty on the airline in May for violations, though details of the earlier penalty were not immediately available.The show-cause notice was issued a day before SpiceJet's board approved a proposal to raise up to Rs 5,500 crore to strengthen its financial position.SpiceJet's domestic market share fell to 0.6% in September from 1.2% in August, as the airline continued to face operational challenges resulting in flight delays and cancellations.Its shares fell nearly 5% to Rs 9.74 in afternoon trade on the BSE. The exchange has also sought clarification from the airline regarding reports of the DGCA show-cause notice.The airline's worsening cash crunch has disrupted operations, with several scheduled flights being cancelled amid mounting financial difficulties.Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport has issued an advisory warning passengers that some SpiceJet flights could be affected and asked them to contact the airline for the latest updates."Please note, due to operational challenges being faced by SpiceJet Airlines, some flights may be impacted. Passengers are requested to contact SpiceJet directly for the latest information regarding their flight status and travel plans. Thank you for your patience and understanding," the airport said.The advisory comes as SpiceJet struggles with mounting flight cancellations and financial woes.Despite receiving DGCA approval to operate around 66 flights daily under the winter schedule, the airline has reportedly been operating barely 15 flights a day while continuing to accept bookings across its published schedule, according to an ET report.For the second consecutive day on Friday, Delhi airport operator DIAL issued a similar advisory on X, warning passengers that some flights could be affected due to operational challenges faced by SpiceJet.
Article Summary: The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has issued a show-cause notice to crisis-hit SpiceJet. The regulator is seeking an explanation for rising flight cancellations, operational disruptions and alleged regulatory violations. SpiceJet has been directed to respond within seven days of the notice.

Article Title: Rupee extends winning run, climbs 17 paise to 93.15 against US dollar
Article Text:
Rupee gains against US dollar in early trade

NEW DELHI: Rupee continued its upward journey for the fifth consecutive session on Friday, gaining 17 paise to trade at 93.15 against the US dollar in early deals. Strong foreign investor buying in Indian equities and a decline in the dollar against major global currencies helped the currency hold its ground, even as crude oil prices moved higher and stock markets remained under pressure.The currency began the session at 93.25 at the interbank foreign exchange market before strengthening to 93.15. Its latest gains follow a 9-paise rise on Thursday, when it closed at 93.32 against the US dollar.Rupee has gained 78 paise, or 0.83%, over the three sessions preceding Thursday, recovering from its November 13 closing level of 94.19.The movement in crude oil, gold and silver prices could influence rupee's trajectory in the coming sessions. Anuj Choudhary from Mirae Asset Sharekhan expects the domestic currency to retain a slightly positive bias, with lower crude oil prices and a sharp correction in precious metal prices potentially easing the country's import bill."Softening of US Treasury yields may also support the rupee. However, a strong dollar and hawkish Fed speak may cap sharp gains. USD-INR spot price is expected to trade in a range of Rs 92.85 to Rs 93.40," he added.The dollar index, which tracks the US currency against six major currencies, slipped 0.07% to 103.76. Brent crude, on the other hand, edged 0.40% higher to $92.35 per barrel in futures trade.Foreign fund inflows continued to provide support to the rupee. Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) purchased domestic equities worth Rs 7,411.41 crore on Thursday, according to exchange data.The buying came even as domestic benchmarks started Friday's session in the red. BSE Sensex was down 217.03 points, or 0.26%, at 82,804.72, while the Nifty shed 58.70 points, or 0.23%, to trade at 25,455.60 in early deals. However, Dalal Street turned green later in the session.
Article Summary: Rupee gains 17 paise to trade at 93.15 against the US dollar in early deals. Strong foreign investor buying in Indian equities and a decline in the dollar against major global currencies helped the currency hold its ground. Brent crude, on the other hand, edged 0.40% higher to $92.35 per barrel in futures trade.

Article Title: Builder cancels Bengaluru woman’s Rs 1.65 crore flat despite taking Rs 16.5 lakh payment and allots it to another buyer who paid 50% value; Karnataka RERA orders Rs 5 lakh compensation for mental agon
Article Text:
A homebuyer who booked an apartment in Bengaluru found herself embroiled in a dispute with the developer. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

Why did RERA rule in favour of the homebuyer?

You book a flat and make part payment for it, and repeatedly follow up for execution of the agreement for sale. Then you discover that the apartment has been allotted to another buyer. What do you do?A homebuyer who booked an apartment in Bengaluru found herself embroiled in a dispute with the developer after alleging that the flat was allotted to another purchaser without her consent.The Karnataka Real Estate Regulatory Authority (K-RERA) has awarded her compensation for the agony. A separate case for refund with interest is pending.The dispute concerned a homebuyer who bought an apartment in the developer’s project. The woman buyer booked a three-bedroom apartment, with a carpet area of 1,270 sq ft and one car parking space. The allotment letter was issued in 2024, and the total sale consideration was Rs 1,64,99,147.70, inclusive of applicable GST.The woman’s case was that she had agreed to pay 10% of the sale consideration during booking, followed by 30% in 2025, with the remaining amount payable according to a construction-linked schedule from 2026 onwards.The homebuyer alleged that the Bengaluru developer cancelled her apartment allotment without informing her and allotted the same flat to another purchaser.The woman buyer alleged that she had paid towards the booking, arranged funds for the remaining consideration and repeatedly followed up for execution of the agreement for sale.The order records that the payment schedule had been discussed with the promoter’s representative and approved in writing. The homebuyer stated that she made the booking payment in accordance with this arrangement.In fact, she sold another property in 2025, for Rs 1,02,71,250, according to the sale deed discussed in the order. She said she needed the proceeds to arrange funds for the apartment.A draft agreement for sale was emailed to her on January 23, 2025, but she alleged that the developer failed to complete the formalities despite repeated follow-ups.On February 12, 2025, she was informed that a fresh payment demand of Rs 57.74 lakh had been raised in place of an earlier demand of Rs 35 lakh. On June 28, 2025, she received an email seeking her bank details to process a refund. Agarwal maintained that she had neither requested cancellation of the allotment nor sought a refund.The dispute took a decisive turn on October 30, 2025, when she visited the project site. According to the complaint, she discovered that the apartment had been re-allotted to a third party and that an agreement had been executed with the new purchaser.The order also records that, on November 18, 2025, she was informed that the flat could not be allotted to her because another customer had paid 50% of the consideration.Agarwal sought Rs 15 lakh for mental agony and Rs 25 lakh for financial loss and loss of opportunity. The developer did not appear before the authority despite notice, and the complaint proceeded ex parte.Karnataka Real Estate Regulatory Authority considered the allotment letter, payment records, email communications and draft agreement.The order noted that the complainant had paid towards the sale consideration but had not received an executed agreement for sale. It also recorded that an agreement concerning the same apartment had been executed in favour of another purchaser.K-RERA treated the developer’s conduct as inconsistent with its contractual commitments and obligations under the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016. In discussing the absence of an executed agreement despite receipt of payment, the order described this as “a clear violation of RERA Act.”Sunitha Rajesh, Partner at CMS Induslaw tells TOI that the K-RERA order highlights some basic but important principles under the RERA Act.However it is important to note this order is ex-parte i.e., passed without having heard the builder.“The decision was based on one-side of the facts, and the decision may undergo a change in an appeal by the builder,” she says.According to Sunitha Rajesh, the three key facts considered by the authority as are under:First, the builder had collected about Rs 16.5 lakh, which exceeded 10% of the flat's sale consideration of Rs 1.65 crore, without executing an agreement for sale. The RERA Act does not permit a promoter to collect more than 10% of the sale consideration before entering into an agreement for sale.Second, the builder raised demands that were not in accordance with the agreed payment schedule. A payment schedule accepted by both parties cannot be altered unilaterally.Third, the apartment was allotted to another purchaser while the buyer's money continued to remain with the builder. The Authority treated this as a unilateral cancellation by the builder and not as refund.“While awarding compensation, the Authority recognised that when a buyer receives only a refund, the buyer loses not only the money paid but also the opportunity to benefit from the property's appreciation,” Sunitha Rajesh says.“For homebuyers, the case reinforces the importance of ensuring that an agreement for sale is executed before making substantial payments. Buyers should also respond promptly and in writing to any cancellation or refund communication or unilateral changes in the terms agreed at the time of allotment that they do not accept,” she adds.Because this order was passed ex-parte, it may be challenged by the builder and may not be the final word in this matter.In an order dated October 7, 2026, RERA directed the builder to pay the homebuyer Rs 5 lakh towards mental agony, financial loss and loss of opportunity. The developer was also directed to pay Rs 7,000 towards litigation costs.If it failed to comply within 60 days, interest at the marginal cost of funds-based lending rate (MCLR) plus 2% per annum would apply from the 61st day until realisation.The judgment separately records that the homebuyer had filed another complaint seeking a refund with interest, which was pending adjudication.Thus, the October 7 order did not direct the developer to refund the amount she had paid towards the apartment.
Article Summary: A homebuyer who booked an apartment in Bengaluru found herself embroiled in a dispute with the developer. She alleged that the flat was allotted to another purchaser without her consent. Karnataka Real Estate Regulatory Authority has awarded her compensation for the agony.

Article Title: Sarvam's Token Factory raises control issue
Article Text:
Token Factory connects a company’s software to several AI model

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Sarvam AI's Token Factory has allowed businesses to use China's DeepSeek and have their requests processed in India. Running DeepSeek alongside its own model on Indian servers raises a question over India's push for sovereign AI. How much control does local hosting give businesses over models trained overseas?Token Factory connects a company's software to several AI models through a single interface, known as an API. Businesses can choose which model handles each request. Sarvam offers own 105B model alongside China's DeepSeek, Kimi and GLM, and Google's Gemma. The company says it runs the models on clusters of graphics processors in India and matches or beats leading global providers on speed and cost for most of models it offers.Atul Arya, founder and CEO of AI services firm Blackstraw, said a model's country of origin deserves scrutiny, particularly from banks and insurers. Businesses should ask whether they can audit and secure the model, control how their data passes through it and understand where it falls short. "If I'm honest, a model from a 'trusted' country that you can't inspect or govern isn't much safer either," Arya said, adding, running a model in India can help regulated businesses address data security and compliance requirements."DeepSeek's Chinese origin is important, but less important than control." said Jaspreet Bindra, co-founder and CEO of AI & Beyond. In DeepSeek's case, he said, the test is whether Sarvam can independently inspect and secure the model, control its updates, set limits on its behaviour and keep critical functions running without relying on a foreign provider.Those capabilities would sit with Sarvam, and customers would still need to know whether their prompts and responses are retained or used for training, who can access the logs and what happens if a model is withdrawn. "Even if the provider has control over fine-tuning, patching and decommissioning the model, customers are still reliant on a third party," said Rajesh Chhabra, GM for India and Asia at cybersecurity firm Acronis.Queries sent to Sarvam remained unanswered.A single interface makes it easier to pick a model for each task, said Manik Nangia, chief business officer at LeadSquared, an AI-powered CRM platform. “What enterprises need most is choice, the ability to use the right model for each task, under Indian data protection requirements, without being locked into a single provider. Sovereignty and flexibility have to go together for this to work at scale," said Nangia.
Article Summary: Sarvam AI's Token Factory has allowed businesses to use China's DeepSeek and have their requests processed in India. The company says it runs the models on clusters of graphics processors in India and matches or beats leading global providers on speed and cost.

Article Title: New Air India CEO briefs Noel, Chandra at Gurugram HQ
Article Text:
Air India is seeking to narrow the gap between operating costs and revenue through network restructuring, lower unit costs and higher passenger yields as it works towards profitability.

MUMBAI/NEW DELHI: Months after Noel Tata, chairman of Tata Trusts and a director of Tata Sons , questioned the financial performance of Air India , he joined fellow Tata Sons directors on a visit to the airline's Gurugram headquarters and training academy on Thursday.The visit, organised by Tata Sons and Air India chairman N Chandrasekaran , was part of a broader effort to give directors deeper insight into the airline's operations, transformation programme and turnaround progress. Trusts vice-chairman and Tata Sons director Venu Srinivasan was the only absentee and is learnt to be in Botswana.Air India's new chief executive, Tewolde Gebremariam outlined the airline's roadmap to profitability, including plans to improve efficiencies, strengthen cost controls and drive greater synergies with Air India Express. Tata Sons directors also visited the airline's operations control centre, housed within the Gurugram campus. The visit came a day ahead of Air India's board meeting on Friday and followed hours of interactions between directors and the airline's senior management team.Air India has drawn scrutiny from Noel over losses and capital allocation. At Tata Sons' Feb board meeting, Noel raised concerns over the performance of Air India and other newer ventures, leading to the deferment of Chandrasekaran's reappointment as chairman.On Nov 14, Noel said he did not question "the direction" of Tata Sons' investments but questioned "the delivery" of those initiatives. Following the Feb board meeting, Chandrasekaran initiated a process under which heads of Air India, Tata Digital and Tata Electronics would present their financial and operational plans directly to the Tata Sons board.He also proposed visits by directors to Air India's Gurugram headquarters, Tata Electronics' semiconductor project at Dholera and Tata Digital's fulfillment and dark-store operations. Former Air India CEO Campbell Wilson, Tata Digital CEO Sajith Sivanandan and Tata Electronics CEO Randhir Thakur subsequently briefed directors on their businesses at Tata Sons board meeting in May. Thursday's visit to Air India's Gurugram facility marks the first board-level operational review under the initiative.Earlier this month, Tewolde said Air India has "punched below its weight" for too long and is mulling a fresh order for more wide body aircraft to "regain market share from competition (foreign airlines)" as that "business belongs to Air India." While the "short term" poses multiple "challenges", the "long term is a huge opportunity" and the airline could be profitable "very soon" by focusing on cutting costs and boosting revenue and efficiency, he said on Nov 3.

Article Title: Pentagon standoff, copyright lawsuit to AI safety concerns: 5 controversies that have put Anthropic under scrutiny
Article Text:
Anthropic's rapid rise has also brought a series of controversies.

The Pentagon standoff

$1.5 billion copyright settlement

Researcher’s ‘end of the world’ warning

Claude and the Venezuela raid

Changes to AI safety commitments

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Anthropic has positioned itself as a safety-focused alternative in an increasingly competitive AI industry, building its reputation around responsible AI development and safeguards against potential misuse.Founded by former OpenAI employees, the company has repeatedly emphasised the need to ensure that increasingly powerful AI systems remain under human control.However, its rapid rise has also brought a series of controversies, ranging from copyright infringement allegations and disagreements with the US government over military applications to concerns about the existential risks of advanced AI.The most high-profile dispute erupted in February 2026, when Anthropic refused to remove restrictions preventing Claude from being used for mass domestic surveillance and fully autonomous lethal weapons. The US department of defence wanted broader authority to use the technology for what it called all lawful purposes.President Donald Trump directed federal agencies to stop using Anthropic’s technology, while defence secretary Pete Hegseth designated the company a national security supply-chain risk.Anthropic challenged the move in court. In September, a US appeals court upheld the Pentagon’s designation in a 2-1 decision, allowing the department to remove Claude from its systems and barring its use for Defence Department work.Anthropic said it disagreed with the appeals court ruling.Anthropic agreed to pay $1.5 billion to settle a class-action lawsuit brought by authors who accused it of downloading pirated books to train its AI models. A US court granted final approval in July 2026. The agreement covers more than 480,000 works allegedly obtained from pirate libraries, including Library Genesis and Pirate Library Mirror.The settlement followed a distinction drawn by a federal judge in 2025, which said that using copyrighted books to train AI models could qualify as fair use, but making and retaining copies of pirated books was not protected by that finding.However, the settlement did not establish that all AI training using copyrighted material is illegal.In September, Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon announced his resignation, warning that AI developers were racing towards self-improving superintelligence without adequately addressing the risks. Coxon, who said he had worked on pretraining research at OpenAI and Anthropic, wrote that companies were “racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives”.He said people building the technology believed it could “kill us all by the end of the decade”. His comments were a warning about future risks, not evidence that existing AI systems have reached that level of capability. His resignation fuelled debate over whether AI development should slow until safeguards improve.Anthropic faced questions after reports that the US military had used Claude during the January 3 operation to capture Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro.The Wall Street Journal reported that the model was used in the mission, but Reuters said it could not independently verify the report. Axios also reported its use during the active operation, while noting that the precise role was unclear.Anthropic said it could not comment on whether Claude had been used in a specific classified operation. The reports drew attention because the company’s restrictions on military use were already at the centre of its dispute with the Pentagon. The tasks Claude performed during the raid have not been publicly established.Anthropic’s safety policies have also come under scrutiny. In February 2026, it substantially rewrote its Responsible Scaling Policy, introducing Frontier Safety Roadmaps and regular risk reports. In July, it changed internal access rules for unredacted risk reports, requiring them to be shared with at least 200 employees rather than all staff with regular security clearance.In October, the company retired a roadmap goal for systematic oversight of training data to assess alignment with Claude’s Constitution. Anthropic said existing reviews were already identifying the issues such checks were designed to catch, and that a later sample review found no additional problems. It said it would reconsider which goals were most effective for alignment.
Article Summary: Anthropic has positioned itself as a safety-focused alternative in an increasingly competitive AI industry. The company has repeatedly emphasised the need to ensure that increasingly powerful AI systems remain under human control. Its rapid rise has also brought a series of controversies, ranging from copyright infringement allegations and disagreements with the US government over military applications.

Article Title: JPMorgan, Visa, Mastercard hit by cyber incidents; data of thousands of customers leaked
Article Text:
JPMorgan Chase is among the affected banks, along with Visa and mastercard

Hackers claim to have accessed thousands of JPMorgan records

Visa, Mastercard confirm separate vendor breaches

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard have disclosed separate cyber incidents involving third-party service providers, with customer information, including thousands of email addresses, exposed in data leaks. The breach at JPMorgan, the largest US lender, appears to have compromised marketing records containing customer names, email addresses and, in some cases, phone numbers and postal codes. All three companies said their payment systems were not affected and no card payment information was exposed.JPMorgan said on Thursday that attackers had targeted vendors providing services to the bank and accessed certain marketing data held by them. The bank said it was investigating the incident and would contact affected customers directly."Based on our investigation so far, we believe the attackers accessed certain marketing data held by those vendors, which may include some customer names and email addresses," a JPMorgan spokesperson said.The bank did not disclose the number of customers affected. The information exposed appears to involve only a small fraction of Chase's tens of millions of customers, according to the Associated Press.The disclosure of leak follows claims by a cyber extortion group called "n0n", which said on November 16 that it had obtained cardmember engagement records from JPMorgan.A Reuters review of data posted by the group found more than 16,000 customer email addresses, some phone numbers and postal codes, as well as what appeared to be 124 bank employee email addresses.The bank clarified that the cyberattack was unrelated to service disruptions earlier this week, when a software bug affected transaction processing at JPMorgan and other banks."There is no connection to service disruption of some customers experienced earlier this week," the spokesperson said.The same hacking group made claims involving Visa and Mastercard on November 16. Both companies confirmed incidents at third-party providers but said their payment networks and customers' ability to use their cards were unaffected.Visa said its incident involved a third-party service provider in the Asia-Pacific region. "Visa’s systems were not involved and were not impacted. No payments data such as card numbers were affected," a spokesperson said.Mastercard said a third-party breach exposed a limited number of email addresses belonging to cardholders enrolled in a specific benefits programme. It described the information as non-payment data and said there was no impact on its payment network."At this time, the exposure has been contained and our teams are working with the provider to support the impacted cardholders as needed," a Mastercard spokesperson said, according to AP.Data posted by the group found purported Visa customer records across several Asia-Pacific markets, including Hong Kong, Taiwan, Japan, Singapore and Australia, as per Reuters. The Mastercard material appeared to contain marketing data related to customers in North America, the Middle East and Africa.The incidents have renewed questions about how much customer information financial companies share with external vendors and how closely they monitor the security of those providers."Customers don't distinguish between a bank and a vendor when it comes to a cyberattack, so there is a question of reputational risk here," said Carissa Robb of consulting firm SolomonEdwards.She said companies needed to face greater scrutiny over how frequently they review the data shared with vendors and whether all of it is necessary.The JPMorgan disclosure comes amid a series of technology disruptions affecting businesses and infrastructure providers. The bank's transaction-processing problems earlier this week also prompted inquiries from US banking regulators, who sought to assess the impact and establish whether the incident was cyber-related.
Article Summary: JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard have disclosed separate cyber incidents involving third-party service providers. Customer information, including thousands of email addresses, exposed in data leaks. All three companies said their payment systems were not affected and no card payment information was exposed. JPMorgan disclosure comes amid a series of technology disruptions affecting businesses and infrastructure providers.

Article Title: Anthropic IPO: AI giant's shares close 17% higher on first day of trading; company valued at $1.76 trillion
Article Text:
Anthropic IPO listing at the NASDAQ MarketSite in Times Square.

Anthropic IPO surpasses SpaceX

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

AI industry faces regulatory scrutiny and public backlash

Also read:

Artificial intelligence company Anthropic made a blockbuster debut on the Nasdaq on Thursday, with its shares closing 17.07% higher at $97.17 after opening more than 30 per cent above their initial public offering (IPO) price.The shares opened at $111.50, against the IPO price of $83, and rose to an intraday high of $115.10 before paring gains. Anthropic's fully diluted market valuation stood at $1.76 trillion at the closing price, after briefly climbing above $2 trillion during the opening minutes of trading.The listing marks the largest IPO on record and comes amid growing investor interest in artificial intelligence companies, despite concerns over a possible AI bubble, high infrastructure costs and the technology's impact on jobs and livelihoods.Anthropic, which is based in San Francisco, trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT.Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share on Wednesday, valuing the company at around $1.5 trillion. The offering made it the largest IPO on record, surpassing SpaceX, which raised about $75 billion in June.The company offered 980 million shares to the public, including shares from the company as well as early investors and existing stockholders.At the IPO price, the offering translates into proceeds of approximately $81 billion.The strong market debut came after robust investor demand for Anthropic shares. The company had initially indicated a price range of $70 to $78 per share but eventually priced the offering above that range.The listing is also a major milestone for the AI industry, with Anthropic among the first major developers of advanced AI models to enter the public markets. Its performance is expected to offer an indication of investor appetite for the sector.Despite the strong market debut, Anthropic faces significant financial challenges. The company has accumulated $6.2 billion in debt, which it described as "substantial" in its financial filings. It is also unprofitable under standard accounting measures, the Associated Press reported.The company's large spending commitments have added to concerns about its ability to generate returns from investments in artificial intelligence infrastructure.Anthropic has signed leases and other agreements that could require it to spend $900 billion on computing power and infrastructure over the coming years, including $70 billion in the next 12 months.Although the company currently has substantial cash reserves, its spending plans could put pressure on its finances if it cannot raise additional funds.Anthropic now has way to raise capital through the stock market rather than relying further on borrowing, which has become more expensive amid inflation concerns and the growing financing requirements of AI companies.The company's listing will also allow employees to sell their vested shares, potentially making many of them millionaires. It could further increase the wealth of chief executive Dario Amodei and his sister and co-founder, Daniela Amodei.Founded in 2021 by former OpenAI executives, Anthropic is competing with OpenAI, Google and several other companies in the race to dominate artificial intelligence.However, the enormous costs of developing AI models and building data centres have raised questions about whether companies can generate sufficient returns on their investments.Anthropic, OpenAI and SpaceX's AI division have all spent more than they have earned, adding to fears of a bubble in the sector.The industry also faces growing public opposition over the expansion of data centres, their resource requirements and concerns about AI's impact on employment.Regulatory pressure could increase once the new US Congress takes office next year. Newly elected Democrats have pledged to tighten oversight of the industry, while Democratic governors-elect in Texas and Georgia have vowed to oppose new data centre construction.Anthropic's rival OpenAI has reportedly been considering a stock market listing in 2027, making the performance of Anthropic's IPO particularly significant for the wider industry.
Article Summary: Anthropic's fully diluted market valuation stood at $1.76 trillion at the closing price, after briefly climbing above $2 trillion during the opening minutes of trading. The offering made it the largest IPO on record, surpassing SpaceX, which raised about $75 billion in June.

Article Title: Oil prices slip as supply concerns and US rate hike fears weigh on market sentiment
Article Text:
Crude prices edge lower

Oil prices edged lower on Thursday, with both major benchmarks trading in the red as expectations of higher supplies and interest rates continued to weigh on the market. Concerns over attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz amid the ongoing Iran war provided some support, limiting the decline.WTI crude futures were trading at $82.92 a barrel, down 34 cents, or 0.41%, while Brent crude stood at $91.93, slipping 2 cents, or 0.02%.The two benchmarks had ended the previous session lower. Brent lost 1.3%, while WTI declined 3.2%, touching its lowest level since August 26. The fall came amid growing expectations of excess supply, with crude shipments through the Strait of Hormuz recovering to levels seen before the war.The possibility of another US interest rate increase has added to the cautious mood in oil markets. Higher borrowing costs could weigh on economic growth and slow the expansion in oil demand. A stronger dollar could further add to the pressure by making crude, which is priced in dollars, more expensive for buyers using other currencies.Minutes of the US Federal Reserve's October meeting, published on Wednesday, reinforced expectations among investors that the central bank could increase interest rates at its December meeting to bring inflation under control."Softer oil prices provide some relief to those concerned about persistent inflationary pressures, although the question is no longer simply whether the Fed will hike rates in December, but by how much. This, in turn, supports the dollar, hindering any attempt by the oil market to rally," analysts at PVM, a brokerage, said in a note dated November 18.The supply outlook also came under pressure after US crude inventories posted a sharper-than-anticipated increase.The US Energy Information Administration (EIA) reported that crude stocks climbed by 3.4 million barrels to 417.8 million barrels in the week ended November 13. This compared with expectations of a rise of just 58,000 barrels in a Reuters poll of analysts.Meanwhile, the possibility of disruptions to oil supplies from the Middle East continues to remain a concern.Iran's navy said three oil tankers travelling east of the Strait of Hormuz had been disabled by mines, Iranian media reported on Wednesday.Investors are also looking towards a trilateral summit involving the leaders of the US, China and Russia for signals on the possibility of a negotiated end to the US-Iran war and Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Both conflicts have caused disruptions in global oil markets.Separately, Ukrainian drone attacks have affected Russia's oil refining capacity. Reuters reported on Wednesday, citing industry sources, that the attacks have cut the combined crude processing volumes of Russian oil refineries by 45% since late October.
Article Summary: Both major benchmarks trading in the red as expectations of higher supplies and interest rates continue to weigh on the market. Concerns over attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz amid the ongoing Iran war provided some support, limiting the decline. Higher borrowing costs could weigh on economic growth and slow the expansion in oil demand.

Article Title: Anthropic surpasses SpaceX with record $81.31 billion IPO, prices shares at $83 apiece
Article Text:
Anthropic makes blockbuster debut at stock market

Heavy spending makes fresh capital important

Anthropic has emerged with the biggest IPO ever, raising $81.31 billion through its stock-market offering and surpassing SpaceX's $75 billion fundraising. The artificial intelligence company priced its shares at $83 apiece on Wednesday (local time), above its initially indicated range of $70-$78.The pricing values the San Francisco-based AI company at $1.5 trillion and reflects strong investor demand despite concerns surrounding the technology sector and the possibility of an AI bubble.Anthropic, the maker of the Claude AI tool, is scheduled to begin trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker symbol "ANT". While its initial plan was to offer 825 million shares, the final offering comprises 980 million shares of Class A common stock.Of the total, 956,351,354 shares are being sold by Anthropic itself, while 23,648,646 shares are being offered by certain existing stockholders.The scale of investor interest comes at a time when the market is dealing with several uncertainties. These include the ouster of Nvidia's CEO, concerns about an AI bubble, the possibility of a regulatory crackdown by a Democratic-led Congress next year and growing anti-AI sentiment among the public.Despite these concerns, Anthropic's pricing indicates that investors remain willing to put money into major AI companies.“This is strong appetite for this major AI IPO in Anthropic, and it’s a big win for the tech sector after a white-knuckle time with Nvidia. The pricing shows strong demand among investors,” said Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co.Its rival OpenAI, meanwhile, is not planning to enter the stock market until next year.Beyond setting an IPO record, the fundraising gives Anthropic an opportunity to secure additional capital without adding to its existing debt burden.The company has already borrowed $6.2 billion, an amount it has described as “substantial” in its financial filings. It is also unprofitable under standard accounting rules, suggesting that its resources to service interest and principal payments are limited.Its financial requirements are particularly significant given the scale of its infrastructure commitments. Of this, $70 billion is due to be spent over the next 12 months.Although the company currently has ample cash, its sizeable spending plans mean those reserves could be used up quickly if it cannot secure additional funding.
Article Summary: Anthropic, maker of the Claude AI tool, is scheduled to begin trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker symbol "ANT" The company has signed leases and other agreements that will require it to spend $900 billion on computing power and infrastructure over the coming years.

Article Title: Nvidia sets record with $65bn Q3 profit
Article Text:
Representative image

Nvidia Corp sought to deliver a clear message during its first earnings update since the departure of long-time leader Jensen Huang: He's not coming back, and the company will be fine without him.Total sales rose 103% to $115.8 billion for the third quarter of fiscal 2027. The champion of semiconductors for artificial intelligence once again exceeded expectations, both in terms of revenue and net income, which reached $65.3 billion.The chip giant boosted its sales forecast for next year and vowed to improve Nvidia's access to critical supplies, while tamping down speculation that Huang might return. The company also added $150 billion to its stock-buyback programme.The shares rose as much as 2.7% to $159.7 on Wednesday after trading got underway in New York. Nvidia's stock has tumbled in recent weeks, battered by the scandal and broader fears that AI spending is poised to slow. It's down about 17% this year."Our supply is growing, our customers and our partners are with us, and employees are committed," interim CEO Colette Kress said during a conference call with analysts Tuesday."We've got this." It was a high-stakes moment for Kress, who took the reins last week after Huang's ouster - a chaotic exit spurred by multiple extramarital affairs and concerns that he was targeted by a Chinese espionage plot.Nvidia has been the largest beneficiary of the AI build-out, and Huang served as the industry's biggest cheerleader. Now the company looks to ensure that its momentum won't be undermined by the controversy swirling around it."The cards of doubt seemed stacked so high. However, from a bird's-eye view it was a solid 3Q27 print," said Daniel Morgan, a senior portfolio manager at Synovus Trust. "The number of concerns surrounding Nvidia shares will most likely keep the shares range-bound." Bloomberg

Article Title: Anthropic IPO: How to buy shares, expected price and risks investors should know
Article Text:
Anthropic prepares to hit stock market

Anthropic IPO price

How can retail investors apply?

Buying Anthropic through mutual funds

Risks

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India)

AI giant Anthropic is preparing for its stock market debut, giving individual investors an opportunity to own a stake in the company behind chatbot Claude. The initial public offering (IPO) is expected to value the company at $1.4 trillion (£1 trillion), making it one of the biggest stock market listings in history.Investor demand is already strong, with reports suggesting that the offering is nearly six times oversubscribed. However, the IPO comes amid volatility in US markets, particularly technology stocks.Here is what investors need to know about the share price, application process and risks before deciding whether to invest.According to the company's prospectus, Anthropic is offering 825 million shares of Class A common stock at an initial price range of $70 to $78 per share. The final price will be decided on Wednesday.The shares will carry voting rights, but all the votes combined will account for only 49.9% of the total voting power. This means investors will not have enough voting rights to force changes in how the company is run.The shares are scheduled to list on the Nasdaq in New York on Thursday. Both individual investors and large institutions will be able to participate.Investors in the UK can subscribe to Anthropic shares through AJ Bell, Hargreaves Lansdown, Robinhood and eToro.The minimum investment differs across platforms.Robinhood and eToro require a minimum investment of $250 (£189), while Hargreaves Lansdown has set the minimum at £250. AJ Bell requires at least £1,000.The application deadlines are 1pm on Wednesday for AJ Bell and 3pm for Hargreaves Lansdown and Robinhood. All three platforms have warned that applications could close earlier without notice.Those who miss the IPO can still buy shares once they begin trading on the Nasdaq. They will also be available through platforms that are not participating in the offering.Direct investment is not the only way to gain exposure to Anthropic. Some funds already hold stakes in the company.In the UK, these include the Baillie Gifford US Growth and Scottish Mortgage investment trusts. Fidelity also has investments in funds available to US investors.After the listing, Anthropic shares are expected to enter some tracker funds, although the timing will vary. Actively managed funds may also choose to buy the stock. This means investors could gain exposure through their existing fund investments without purchasing shares directly.Strong demand does not necessarily mean the shares will deliver lasting returns. Anthropic's prospectus includes 92 pages detailing potential risks to the company and its industry. Recent volatility in US markets, particularly technology stocks, is another factor investors need to consider.The company's governance structure has also attracted scrutiny. The Guardian's financial editor Nils Pratley has raised concerns, saying it “represents an extraordinary concentration of power in the hands of a few individuals”.Jason Hollands, managing director of investment platform Bestinvest by Evelyn Partners, which is not participating in the IPO, has also highlighted concerns about the company's profitability.“Anthropic would give most retail investors the first opportunity to have a direct stake in a frontier AI developer. But it remains a capital-intensive business, and it has yet to establish a consistent path to profitability,” he told The Guardian. “Investors will need to judge whether the company can turn demand for its models into durable earnings.”Hollands says strong demand and limited share supply could push up the stock initially, but that does not guarantee sustained gains.
Article Summary: Anthropic is offering 825 million shares of Class A common stock at an initial price range of $70 to $78 per share. The shares are scheduled to list on the Nasdaq in New York on Thursday. Both individual investors and large institutions will be able to participate.
